title: Snapshot attestation replayer for cross-region residency & KMS proofs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an automated 'snapshot attestation replayer' service that reconstructs object lifecycle and key events to produce tamper-evident evidence bundles for audits. The service will correlate storage object snapshots, retention-policy changes, and KMS/HSM key rotation logs across regions, then replay and sign a chronological proof bundle a verifier can consume. This targets SOC/ISO audit requests where auditors require contiguous, queryable proofs tying a data object's residency and retention state to the specific encryption keys active at each point in time.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype replayer ingests S3-style object events, retention policy change logs, and KMS rotation entries for a 30-day window
Attestation bundle format defined and documented (JSON+signed manifest) with schema and example
Bundle includes canonicalized timeline entries with references to storage object IDs, region tags, retention policy IDs, and key version identifiers
Bundles are cryptographically signed using an internal audit signing key and verification tooling validates signatures and timeline consistency
Integration tests that inject synthetic events and validate end-to-end bundle generation and verification
Dashboard tile in Console shows per-bundle status (generated/verified/failed) and per-customer throughput
tasks: Design canonical timeline schema and proof manifest (owner: Luca)
Build event ingestor for storage events (owner: infra-team)
Adaptor for KMS/HSM rotation streams and mapping to key versions (owner: crypto-team)
Retention-change extractor from Console audit logs (owner: console-team)
Bundle assembler service with signing endpoint (owner: evidence-service)
Verification CLI and lightweight verifier library for auditors (owner: sec-eng)
Add observability: metrics, SLOs, and Console tile (owner: monitoring)
Create runbook and disaster-recovery steps for replayer (owner: oncall)
Write integration tests and load tests to simulate cross-region bursts (owner: qa)
Document API and provide sample audit queries in Confluence and Drive (owner: technical-writer)
decisions: Use a signed manifest approach instead of storing full event payloads in proof bundle to keep bundle size manageable
Canonicalize timestamps to UTC and include observed-offsets to make timeline comparable across region clocks
Signer will be an internal non-rotating audit key with a rotating subordinate key for operational signing to balance audit traceability and key hygiene
Replayer will operate on immutable event logs (object snapshots, KMS audit streams) rather than live state to avoid race conditions
risks: Event gaps: incomplete ingestion could produce partial bundles that look inconsistent to auditors
Clock skew across regions could break chronological assertions if not normalized
Signing key management: storing an always-available audit signer increases attack surface unless properly isolated
Performance: reconstructing long timelines for high-churn buckets may be CPU/memory intensive
comments: 2025-03-02 - Priya Shah (PM): Include requirement to tie retention policy ID snapshots to the Console's retention change API. Auditors ask for policy lineage.
2025-03-05 - Marcus Liu (Crypto): Prefer using an HSM-wrapped subordinate signing key that is rotated nightly; main audit root kept offline and used only for quarterly notarization.
2025-03-08 - Elmira Petrova (Privacy): Confirm PII handling in bundles — we should never include raw payloads. Only references and digests are allowed.
